title: Describe, apply, analyse and calculate shape and motion in 2-and 3-dimensional space in different contexts

lessons.title: Perimeter and area of 2-D shapes
lessons.html:
Measuring flat shapes

Team leaders and supervisors calculate lengths and areas when planning fencing, floor space in a packhouse, pallet layouts or planted blocks on a farm.

Perimeter

Perimeter is the distance around a shape.

  • Rectangle: P = 2 × (length + width).
  • Circle (circumference): C = π × diameter, or 2 × π × radius, with π ≈ 3.14.

Example: a camp 120 m long and 80 m wide needs 2 × (120 + 80) = 400 m of fencing per strand. A 3-strand fence needs 1 200 m of wire.

Area

Area is the amount of flat surface, measured in square units (m², ha).

ShapeFormula
RectangleA = length × width
TriangleA = ½ × base × perpendicular height
CircleA = π × radius²
TrapeziumA = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height

Example: an orchard block of 250 m × 160 m = 40 000 m² = 4 ha (since 1 ha = 10 000 m²).

Example: a centre-pivot circle with radius 300 m has area 3.14 × 300 × 300 = 282 600 m², about 28.3 ha.

Composite shapes

Irregular areas, such as an L-shaped cold store floor, can be split into rectangles and triangles. Calculate each part and add them.

Using area in practice

  • Floor space: how many pallets (1.2 m × 1.0 m) fit in a 12 m × 10 m cold room, allowing aisles.
  • Paint or sealant: area of walls to be coated, divided by coverage per litre on the product label.
  • Planting density: trees per hectare from row spacing × in-row spacing. At 6 m × 3 m, each tree occupies 18 m², so about 10 000 ÷ 18 ≈ 555 trees per hectare.

lessons.title: Volume and surface area of 3-D objects
lessons.html:
Measuring solid shapes

Volume

Volume is the space inside a 3-D object, measured in cubic units (m³, cm³) or litres. 1 m³ = 1 000 L; 1 000 cm³ = 1 L.

ObjectFormulaWorkplace example
Rectangular prism (box)V = length × width × heightCarton, cold room, bulk bin
CylinderV = π × r² × hWater tank, silo, drum
ConeV = ⅓ × π × r² × hSilo hopper, heap of grain

Example: a cold room 8 m × 6 m × 3 m has a volume of 144 m³.

Example: a round water tank with diameter 2 m and height 2.5 m. Radius = 1 m. Volume = 3.14 × 1 × 1 × 2.5 = 7.85 m³ = 7 850 L.

Capacity and mass

For bulk materials, mass = volume × density. Densities differ by product and moisture, so use figures supplied by your operation. If a silo holds a known volume and grain has a known bulk density, you can estimate tons stored.

Surface area

Surface area is the total area of all faces of a 3-D object. It is used to calculate packaging material, insulation or paint.

  • Box: SA = 2(lw + lh + wh).
  • Cylinder: SA = 2πr² + 2πrh.

Example: a carton 0.5 m × 0.3 m × 0.25 m has SA = 2(0.15 + 0.125 + 0.075) = 2 × 0.35 = 0.7 m² of board, before allowing for flaps and overlaps.

Scale and plans

Plans and maps use scale. On a 1:500 plan, 1 cm represents 500 cm (5 m). A building 4.2 cm long on the plan is 21 m long in reality. When length is scaled by a factor k, area scales by k² and volume by k³: doubling the dimensions of a bin gives eight times the volume.

lessons.title: Position, motion and speed
lessons.html:
Describing position and movement

Position

Location can be described with grid references on a farm map, compass directions (N, S, E, W) and bearings measured clockwise from north, or GPS coordinates. Emergency services need precise locations, so team leaders should know the GPS pin or clear directions to their workplace.

Transformations

  • Translation: sliding without turning, like cartons on a conveyor.
  • Rotation: turning about a point, like a rotary sizer or a fan; a full rotation is 360°.
  • Reflection: a mirror image, like left and right sides of a carcass or symmetrical packaging layouts.
  • Enlargement: scaling a shape larger or smaller, as on plans.

Speed, distance and time

Speed = distance ÷ time. Distance = speed × time. Time = distance ÷ speed.

Example: a truck travels 180 km to the port at an average 60 km/h. Time = 180 ÷ 60 = 3 hours.

Example: a conveyor belt moves at 0.5 m/s. A carton travels 15 m to the palletiser in 15 ÷ 0.5 = 30 seconds.

Rotational motion

For wheels and pulleys, distance travelled per revolution equals circumference. A wheel with diameter 0.8 m travels 3.14 × 0.8 = 2.51 m per turn. At 40 revolutions per minute, that is about 100 m per minute.

Pulley and gear ratios change speed: a small driving pulley turning a large driven pulley reduces speed but increases turning force.

Safety with motion

Rotating shafts, belts, pulleys and conveyors create nip points that can trap fingers, hair and clothing. Guards must remain in place. Machines must be stopped and locked out before adjustment or cleaning. Never reach across moving belts.

Key points

  • Perimeter is distance around; area is surface, in m² or ha.
  • Volume of a box = l × w × h; of a cylinder = π × r² × h; 1 m³ = 1 000 L.
  • Surface area is used for packaging, paint and insulation.
  • On scale drawings, area scales by k² and volume by k³.
  • Speed = distance ÷ time; one wheel revolution travels one circumference.
  • Keep guards on moving parts and lock out before cleaning.
